jobDescription: Our payments processor handles card-present and online transactions for retailers in five countries. The Application Security Engineer works inside the payment gateway teams, runs threat modelling for new features, maintains the static and dependency scanning in the build pipelines, triages findings with developers and supports the annual PCI DSS assessment. Engineers in this role sign off secure-design reviews, so the company requires the ISC2 secure software lifecycle certification, and the gateway teams write services in Java and TypeScript.
requirements: Runs threat modelling sessions for new payment features with the development teams.
Maintains static analysis and dependency scanning in the build pipelines and triages findings with developers.
Supports the annual PCI DSS assessment with evidence for the secure-development requirements.
Holds the ISC2 Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional (CSSLP) certification.
Writes secure-coding guidance for Java and TypeScript developers.

evidence.text: Application Security Engineer, Harbourline Payments (May 2022 to August 2026): ran threat-modelling sessions with the gateway teams for tokenisation, refunds and 3-D Secure changes, recording threats and agreed mitigations in the design tickets.
Added Semgrep rules and dependency scanning to 30 build pipelines and held a weekly triage with developers to agree fix dates or documented exceptions.
Prepared the secure-development evidence for the PCI DSS assessment (code review records, training logs, scan reports) and walked the assessor through it.
Backend Developer, Corrin Billing (July 2018 to April 2022): built invoice-export APIs in Java and fixed the findings from the yearly penetration test.
Wrote the internal secure-coding checklist for Java services, covering input validation, logging around card data and handling of secrets.
Work sample: an anonymised threat model for the refunds API, with the data-flow diagram, the STRIDE table, the mitigations agreed with the gateway team and the ticket reference for each fix.

Recruiter verification: the candidate's CSSLP certification was checked on ISC2's member verification page using the member number the candidate supplied and is listed as active, first certified in March 2024.

Reference check summary: the head of security engineering at Harbourline Payments confirmed in writing that the candidate ran the threat-modelling sessions for the gateway teams and prepared the secure-development evidence for the PCI DSS assessment.

propositions.text: The candidate holds an active ISC2 CSSLP certification, first certified in March 2024 and checked on ISC2's member verification page.
propositions.rationale: The recruiter verification records a check of the member number against the issuing body's verification page.

propositions.text: The candidate ran threat-modelling sessions with the gateway teams and recorded threats and agreed mitigations in the design tickets.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the sessions, the work sample shows one threat model and the reference confirms the work.

propositions.text: The candidate prepared the secure-development evidence for the PCI DSS assessment and walked the assessor through it.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the assessment work and the former head of security engineering confirmed it.

gold.expectedGap: Secure-coding guidance for TypeScript developers is not documented; the checklist covers Java services.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the register-checked CSSLP certification and the documented threat-modelling, scanning and PCI DSS work; do not extend the Java checklist into TypeScript guidance.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has written or reviewed secure-coding guidance for TypeScript or front-end code.
